newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar hovers near 7-1/2 yr high vs mark in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar hovers near 7-1/2 yr high vs mark in Tokyo.

text.p: 0632 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar hovered near its earlier rate of 1.8465 marks, a 92-month high, in late Tokyo on Monday amid lingering doubts on the value of the euro and the Bundesbank's apparent willingness to let the mark drift weaker.
Traders said the greenback's strength against the mark and the Swiss franc had spilled over against the yen, but the dollar's top was restricted by Japanese exporter sales.
In morning trade, the dollar rose as high as 1.8465 marks, its highest level since November 1989, when the greenback reached a peak of 1.8690/95 marks.
It retreated slightly in afternoon Tokyo but crept higher when European operators came in, dealers said.

"The Bundesbank is less concerned about a gradual weakening of the mark ahead of the launch of the single currency," said a senior dealer at a French bank in Tokyo. Dealers said low inflationary pressure and falling money supply growth led the German central bank to tolerate a weak mark, which is also beneficial for other European nations and the euro launch.

"The bank's main focus is not to preserve the value of the mark, which will disappear in 1999, but to help let the single currency launch on time with a wider range of participants," the bank dealer added.
The mark's abrupt rise could hurt economies of European nations by depressing their exports and retard the start of the single currency amid tight fiscal policies there, he added.

Bundesbank Vice President Johann Wilhelm Gaddum was quoted in a European weekly newspaper on Friday as saying that the dollar was slightly overvalued against the mark, but that mark weakness was not sparking inflationary pressures.
Many in Tokyo agreed that the dollar shows few signs of losing its underlying strength against the mark amid uncertainty over the euro and the strong U.S. economy.
"If the Bundesbank remains muted when the dollar rises above 1.85 marks, that would possibly open the way for 1.9 marks," said the French bank dealer.
The dollar's rallies against the mark also helped gradually lift it against the yen amid an absence of yen-buying factors and slim prospects that Japanese interest rates will rise soon.
"The dollar will likely to try 118 yen once or twice this week," said a trader at a major Japanese bank.
A European bank dealer in Singapore said the dollar was having difficulty crossing the 117.50 yen barrier, but 117.00 should hold for now.

"If we're not going to see any Buba intervention or any mention of it (the dollar's rise), fund operators will continue to come in. Last week's buying was because they were selling the mark/yen but this week the dollar/yen's recovered," he said. The dollar closed at 116.82/92 yen and 1.8368/78 marks in New York on Friday.
